name: Jaguar
mustRead: stocky muscular build on short legs
rosettes with spots inside them
massive broad blocky jaw
note: often drawn as a leopard; the jaguar is far heavier-headed and its rosettes contain central spots

name: Leopard
mustRead: long thick tail nearly as long as the body
hollow ring rosettes with empty centres
low-slung slender body
note: rosettes are open rings with no spot in the middle, unlike a jaguar's

name: Tiger
mustRead: vertical black stripes over orange
white cheek ruff and white eyebrow spots
long ringed tail
note: stripes are vertical on the flank and continue onto the skin, not just a few token bands

name: Clouded Leopard
mustRead: large cloud-shaped dark-edged blotches
tail as long as head and body combined
very short stout legs
note: the tail equals the whole head-body length; drawings usually make it far too short

name: Ocelot
mustRead: chain-like rosettes running in streaks along the flank
two black stripes on each cheek
housecat-sized build with a shortish tail

name: Tapir
mustRead: short flexible prehensile snout
rounded high rump with a sloping back
stubby nub of a tail
note: generic representative: a lowland tapir. Not a pig - the nose is a short mobile proboscis, not a flat disc snout

name: Forest Elephant
mustRead: trunk reaching the ground
straight downward-pointing tusks
rounded ears smaller than a savanna elephant's
note: smaller and darker than the savanna elephant, with straighter tusks and oval ears

name: Gorilla
mustRead: peaked skull crest over a heavy brow ridge
barrel chest with a wide pot belly
knuckle-walking on folded hands
note: arms are markedly longer than the legs, so the shoulders sit higher than the hips

name: Chimpanzee
mustRead: large protruding round ears
flat face with a heavy brow and pale muzzle
long arms reaching past the knees

name: Orangutan
mustRead: shaggy long orange-red hair
enormous arm span with short bowed legs
wide cheek flanges on adult males

name: Wild Boar
mustRead: high shoulder hump sloping down to a low rump
upward-curving tusks from the lower jaw
bristly mane along the spine
note: front-heavy wedge silhouette; not the round barrel body of a farm pig

name: Peccary
mustRead: straight downward-pointing tusks
pig-like body on slim delicate legs
no visible tail
note: tusks point straight down, not curled upward like a boar's

name: Okapi
mustRead: horizontal white stripes on the hindquarters and upper legs
deep chocolate body with a sloping back
giraffe-like head with short skin-covered ossicones
note: a short-necked giraffe relative, not a zebra; only the rear half is striped

name: Sloth
mustRead: long hooked scythe claws
small round flat face with a faint smile
shaggy coarse greenish fur
note: generic representative: a three-toed sloth. Normally hangs upside down beneath a branch, so the limbs read above the body

name: Giant Anteater
mustRead: long tapered tubular snout with a pin-hole mouth
enormous bushy flag-like tail
black-and-white diagonal shoulder wedge
note: walks on the knuckles of the forefeet to keep the huge claws curled inward

name: Capuchin
mustRead: dark cap of hair over a pale pink face
long curling prehensile tail
small slender body with pale shoulders

name: Howler Monkey
mustRead: swollen bearded throat pouch
thick prehensile tail with a bare gripping tip
hunched stocky shoulders and short muzzle

name: Spider Monkey
mustRead: extremely long spindly limbs
prehensile tail longer than the whole body
small round head with a pot belly
note: the hands have no functional thumb - they are hooks

name: Tamarin
mustRead: squirrel-sized body with a long thin tail
facial mane, crest or drooping moustache
clawed fingers gripping a thin branch
note: generic representative: a cotton-top / emperor tamarin type. The tail is long but NOT prehensile

name: Kinkajou
mustRead: long prehensile tail thick at the base
round teddy-bear face with huge dark eyes
golden-brown woolly fur
note: a raccoon relative, not a monkey; it is the only carnivoran in the Americas with a truly prehensile tail

name: Coati
mustRead: long upturned flexible snout
faintly banded tail held straight up like a flagpole
long low body with plantigrade feet

name: Civet
mustRead: masked face with dark bands through the eyes
long ringed or banded tail
low elongated body on short legs
note: generic representative: an Asian palm/common civet. Not a cat - the muzzle is long and pointed

name: Pangolin
mustRead: overlapping keratin scales like a pinecone
thick tapering tail as long as the body
tiny smooth conical head with no visible teeth
note: the head and belly are bare skin; only the back, flanks and tail are scaled

name: Fruit Bat
mustRead: broad membranous wings with visible finger bones
fox-like face with a long muzzle and big eyes
clawed thumb at the bend of the wing
note: no leaf-nose and no huge ears - fruit bats look like winged foxes, not the crinkle-faced insect bats

name: Macaw
mustRead: tail streamer far longer than the body
huge pale hooked beak
bare white facial patch traced with fine feather lines
note: perched in side profile it is much taller than wide because the tail hangs vertically

name: Parrot
mustRead: short deeply hooked beak with a fleshy cere
zygodactyl feet, two toes forward two back
compact stocky body with a short squared tail
note: generic representative: an Amazon-type parrot

name: Toucan
mustRead: oversized brightly banded bill nearly as long as the body
black body with a vivid yellow-white bib
bare blue skin ringing the eye
note: the bill is huge but very light and slightly downcurved, not a straight cone

name: Hornbill
mustRead: huge downcurved bill topped by a hollow casque
long broad tail
bare coloured throat and eye skin with long lashes

name: Hummingbird
mustRead: needle-thin bill at least as long as the head
narrow blade-like wings blurred in a hover
iridescent throat gorget
note: the feet are tiny and tucked; hummingbirds hover with the body held near-vertical, not horizontal

name: Kingfisher
mustRead: dagger bill disproportionately long and straight
oversized head with no visible neck
stubby body and very short tail

name: Eagle
mustRead: heavy hooked beak with a fleshy cere
bony brow ridge giving a scowling glare
massive feathered legs ending in taloned feet
note: generic representative: a large booted eagle. Perched, the folded wings reach roughly to the tail tip

name: Owl
mustRead: flat round facial disc
enormous forward-facing eyes
upright barrel body with no visible neck
note: the 'ear tufts' are feathers, not ears; the wings fold flat against the body and the tail barely projects

name: Anaconda
mustRead: massively thick muscular body
eyes and nostrils set high on top of the head
dark oval blotches over olive-green skin
note: the heaviest snake - the body must read as thick as a thigh, not as a rope

name: Boa
mustRead: saddle-shaped dorsal blotches that redden toward the tail
heavy arrow-shaped head with a dark eye stripe
thick body tapering to a short tail
note: generic representative: a boa constrictor

name: Python
mustRead: net-like geometric blotched pattern
row of heat-sensing pits along the lips
heavy-bodied overlapping coils
note: generic representative: a reticulated/Burmese python type

name: Caiman
mustRead: bony ridge between the eyes
heavily scuted armoured back and neck
broad blunt snout with the teeth hidden when shut
note: snout is broad and rounded like an alligator's; the lower teeth do not show when the mouth is closed

name: Crocodile
mustRead: long narrow V-shaped snout
enlarged fourth lower tooth visible with the jaws shut
double-crested laterally flattened tail
note: teeth interlock and stay visible when the mouth is closed, unlike an alligator's

name: Tree Frog
mustRead: large round adhesive toe pads
bulging eyes set high on the head
long hind legs folded into tight Z-shapes
note: generic representative: a red-eyed / hylid tree frog. The toe discs are the diagnostic feature

name: Poison Dart Frog
mustRead: tiny smooth body in vivid warning colours
bold contrasting blotches or stripes
rounded blunt snout with jet-black eyes
note: very small and smooth-skinned - no warts, no webbing, no toe discs of any size

name: Leafcutter Ant
mustRead: three-part body with a pinched narrow waist
elbowed antennae
spined thorax carrying a leaf fragment overhead
note: the thorax bears distinct backward-pointing spines; the head is oversized with big cutting jaws

name: Butterfly
mustRead: two pairs of broad scaled wings
clubbed knob-tipped antennae
coiled watch-spring proboscis
note: six legs attach only to the thorax, and the antennae end in clubs, not the feathery plumes of a moth

name: Tarantula
mustRead: eight thick densely hairy legs
two-part body: fused cephalothorax plus a bulbous abdomen
downward-stabbing fangs flanked by leg-like pedipalps
note: no antennae and no separate head; the front section carries all eight legs plus the pedipalps

name: Elephant
mustRead: trunk reaching the ground with two grasping lips
huge fan-shaped ears
pillar legs and a dipped saddle back
note: generic representative: an African savanna elephant - big ears, dipped back, both sexes tusked

name: Rhinoceros
mustRead: horn (or two) rising from the nose, not the forehead
thick plated hide with deep folds
barrel body carried low on stumpy three-toed legs
note: the horn grows from the nose; small eyes sit far back on the sides of the head

name: Gaur
mustRead: tall muscular ridge running along the shoulders
white stockings on all four legs
pale grey forehead patch between upcurving horns

name: Banteng
mustRead: white rump patch and white lower legs
white band above the muzzle
smooth crescent horns joined by a bald forehead plate

name: Water Buffalo
mustRead: enormous swept-back crescent horns
heavy low-slung body with a straight back
broad flat wet muzzle held low

name: Deer
mustRead: branched sweeping antlers
slender legs and a long thin neck
large upright cupped ears
note: generic representative: a red / white-tailed deer type. Antlers are branched bone shed each year and only males carry them

name: Antelope
mustRead: unbranched ringed horns swept back or lyre-shaped
deep chest on very fine legs
short flicking tail and tan flank with a white belly
note: generic representative: an impala/gazelle-type antelope. Horns are permanent and unbranched, not deer antlers

name: Sloth Bear
mustRead: shaggy unkempt black coat with a shoulder mane
pale U or Y-shaped chest blaze
long pale mobile snout with huge curved claws
note: the muzzle is long, grey and flexible with protrusible lips - unlike any other bear's short face

name: Macaque
mustRead: bare pink or red face with a short muzzle
short to medium tail
stocky dog-postured body on all fours
note: generic representative: a rhesus/bonnet macaque type

name: Langur
mustRead: tail far longer than the body
black face and hands framed by pale grey fur
slender long-limbed build with a crest on the crown
note: generic representative: a grey/Hanuman langur

name: Mongoose
mustRead: very long low tubular body on short legs
pointed tapering snout with small round ears
thick tail tapering to a point
note: generic representative: an Indian grey mongoose

name: Jackal
mustRead: large pointed erect ears
slender fox-like muzzle
bushy dark-tipped tail carried low
note: generic representative: a golden/black-backed jackal - lighter and leggier than a wolf

name: Porcupine
mustRead: long banded quills laid back over the rump
blunt rounded rodent snout
stocky body carried low with a short quilled tail
note: generic representative: an Old World crested porcupine. Quills are longest over the hips, not evenly spiky like a hedgehog

name: Squirrel
mustRead: bushy plumed tail arched up over the back
sitting on the haunches holding food in the forepaws
large dark eye and rounded ears
note: generic representative: a tree squirrel; the arched tail makes it read taller than long

name: Peacock
mustRead: extremely long trailing train covered in eyespots
fan-shaped crest of wire-tipped feathers
iridescent blue neck and breast
note: the 'tail' is a train of upper tail coverts and only the male has it; unfanned it drags behind, making the bird very long

name: Cobra
mustRead: flared hood spread behind the head
front third of the body reared vertically
coiled base with a fixed lidless stare
note: the hood is spread ribs, not a collar; the reared cobra is taller than it is wide

name: Monitor Lizard
mustRead: long deeply forked flicking tongue
laterally flattened tail longer than the body
muscular sprawled limbs with large hooked claws
note: the neck is long and snake-like, unlike the neckless build of most lizards

name: Pond Turtle
mustRead: low flattened domed shell with a scute mosaic
webbed clawed feet
head extended forward on a wrinkled neck
note: generic representative: a freshwater slider/terrapin type; the shell is low and streamlined, not high-domed like a tortoise

name: Bullfrog
mustRead: large circular eardrum disc behind the eye
very wide flat mouth line
powerful folded hind legs with webbed feet
note: smooth-skinned with no dorsal ridges; the tympanum is bigger than the eye in males

name: Termite
mustRead: pale soft translucent segmented body
straight bead-string antennae
broad joint where the abdomen meets the thorax
note: workers are blind and unpigmented; there is no wasp waist and the antennae are straight, unlike an ant's elbowed pair

name: Cicada
mustRead: broad transparent veined wings tented roof-like over the body
blunt wide head with eyes pushed to the corners
short stout barrel body
note: wings are held tent-like over the back at rest, not spread flat

name: Mantis
mustRead: spined raptorial forelegs folded in prayer
triangular head that swivels on a neck
long slender prothorax raising the front of the body
note: only a mantis truly has a neck - the head turns independently of the body

name: Lion
mustRead: full mane framing the head and shoulders (males)
black tuft at the tail tip
plain tawny coat with a level back
note: the tail tuft is unique among big cats; females have no mane at all

name: Giraffe
mustRead: enormously long neck
skin-covered ossicone horns on the crown
back sloping steeply from high shoulders down to the hips
note: far taller than long - the only common land animal that must be drawn portrait rather than landscape

name: Zebra
mustRead: bold black-and-white stripes continuing onto the legs and belly
stiff upright brush mane
tufted tail with a bare upper half
note: the mane stands erect - it does not flow like a horse's, and the tail is tufted, not full-length hair

name: Kudu
mustRead: towering corkscrew spiral horns
6-10 thin white vertical stripes on the flank
enormous rounded satellite-dish ears
note: the horns make it far taller than a typical antelope; only males carry them

name: Impala
mustRead: lyre-shaped ringed horns curving out then up
vertical black stripes down each side of the white rump
extremely fine legs with a black tuft above the hind hoof

name: Warthog
mustRead: upward-curving tusks and fleshy facial warts
erect bristly mane along the neck and spine
thin tufted tail carried straight up
note: the head is large, flat-fronted and wedge-like; the body is leggier than a domestic pig's

name: Buffalo
mustRead: horns fused into a solid helmet boss across the forehead
massive shoulders and thick neck
large fringed drooping ears hanging below the horns
note: generic representative: an African Cape buffalo

name: Hyena
mustRead: back sloping steeply down from high shoulders to low hindquarters
large rounded ears
thick neck with massive bone-crushing jaws
note: generic representative: a spotted hyena. The forelegs are genuinely longer than the hind legs - the slope is skeletal, not a crouch

name: Baboon
mustRead: long dog-like muzzle with close-set eyes
tail kinked sharply upward at the base then hanging down
cape of long hair over the shoulders in males
note: the tail has a distinctive broken/kinked profile, not a smooth curve

name: Meerkat
mustRead: standing bolt upright, propped on the hind legs and tail
dark rings around the eyes
thin tapering tail with a black tip
note: much taller than wide when sentinel-standing; the ears are small and set low on the sides of the head

name: Caracal
mustRead: long black tufts trailing from the ear tips
plain unmarked reddish-tan coat
long powerful hind legs with a short tail

name: Vulture
mustRead: bare unfeathered head and neck
hunched shoulders above a thick feather ruff
heavy hooked tearing beak
note: generic representative: an Old World griffon-type vulture; perched it hunches with the head drawn into the ruff

name: Guineafowl
mustRead: tiny bare blue-and-red head with a bony helmet casque
round hunched body densely speckled with white dots
thin naked neck on a heavy body
note: the head is comically small for the body and the tail droops downward

name: Viper
mustRead: broad triangular head sharply set off from a thin neck
short thick heavy body
zigzag or diamond dorsal chain pattern
note: generic representative: a European adder / pit-viper type; the pupils are vertical slits and the coil sits low and flat

name: Tortoise
mustRead: tall domed shell with pyramid-growth scutes
columnar elephantine scaly legs
blunt beaked head on a wrinkled retractable neck
note: the feet are stumpy and clubbed with no webbing, unlike a turtle's

name: Locust
mustRead: hugely enlarged folded hind jumping legs
long narrow wings folded flat along the back
short antennae and a tall flat-sided head
note: antennae are short - long thread antennae belong to katydids and crickets, not locusts

name: Dung Beetle
mustRead: glossy armoured domed black body
flat spade-shaped head used as a rake
toothed rake-like digging forelegs
note: many species carry a horn on the head or thorax; the wing cases are smooth and hard, not textured

name: Scorpion
mustRead: pincer claws held forward on long arms
segmented tail arched over the back ending in a sting
flat broad body on eight legs
note: the eyes are tiny and sit on top of the carapace - the pincers, not the face, carry the expression

name: Spectacled Bear
mustRead: pale cream rings or patches around the eyes
shaggy blackish coat
short rounded face with a heavy muzzle
note: the 'spectacle' markings vary and may extend down the chest; some individuals have almost none

name: Mountain Tapir
mustRead: short flexible prehensile snout
thick woolly black coat
white-rimmed lips and a stocky arched back
note: the only long-haired tapir - it should read as woolly, not smooth-skinned

name: Cougar
mustRead: very long heavy black-tipped tail
completely plain unmarked tawny coat
small round head with black muzzle bars
note: no spots, no mane, no rosettes - the plainness is the identity; the hindquarters sit higher than the shoulders

name: Possum
mustRead: naked scaly rat-like prehensile tail
pointed white face with a pink nose
grizzled grey shaggy coat and thin bare ears
note: read as the Virginia opossum; the tail is bare and scaly, not furred like an Australian possum's

name: Tanager
mustRead: short conical seed-crushing bill
brilliantly saturated block-coloured plumage
compact songbird body with a squared tail
note: generic representative: a scarlet/tropical tanager - a small perching songbird, roughly sparrow-sized

name: Tree Snake
mustRead: extremely slender whip-thin body
large eyes with a long pointed snout
body draped in loose loops across branches
note: generic representative: a vine/green tree snake. The body is startlingly thin - pencil-width even at a metre long

name: Anole
mustRead: extendable coloured throat fan (dewlap)
tail longer than the head and body together
adhesive toe pads on long slender limbs
note: generic representative: a green/Carolina anole; the pointed wedge head is longer and narrower than a gecko's

name: Glass Frog
mustRead: translucent belly showing heart and gut
lime-green translucent upperside
forward-facing pale gold eyes
note: the eyes point forward, not sideways, and the underside must read as see-through

name: Salamander
mustRead: moist smooth scaleless skin
four short splayed limbs of roughly equal size
long rounded tail as long as the body
note: generic representative: a fire/spotted salamander. Not a lizard - no scales, no claws, and the toes are soft and blunt

name: Orchid Bee
mustRead: brilliant metallic green, blue or gold body
extremely long tongue trailing back beneath the body
swollen polished hind tibia on males
note: shiny and jewel-like rather than fuzzy - it should not read as a striped honeybee

name: Land Snail
mustRead: coiled spiral shell carried on the back
two pairs of tentacles, the upper pair tipped with eyes
muscular gliding foot with a rippling sole
note: the eyes sit at the very tips of the long upper tentacles, not on the head

name: Panda
mustRead: black teardrop eye patches on a white face
black shoulder band joining black forelegs
round bulky body with a very round head
note: the tail is short but white and visible; the ears are black and round

name: Red Panda
mustRead: long bushy tail with pale rings
white face mask with rust tear-stripes below the eyes
rusty-red coat with jet-black legs and belly
note: raccoon-sized, not bear-sized, and unrelated to the giant panda

name: Asian Elephant
mustRead: twin-domed forehead with a dip between
small triangular ears
convex arched back and a single-lipped trunk tip
note: the back is humped/convex where an African elephant's dips, and the ears are far smaller

name: Takin
mustRead: horns sweeping outward then back like a wildebeest's
humped shoulders on short thick legs
long shaggy golden coat with an arched Roman-nosed muzzle
note: a goat-antelope built like a small bison - far stockier than any goat

name: Pika
mustRead: round egg-shaped body with no visible tail
large round pale-rimmed ears
very short legs holding the belly close to the rock
note: a lagomorph, but the ears are short and round - not long like a rabbit's - and there is no visible tail

name: Pheasant
mustRead: extremely long pointed barred tail
red bare facial wattle around the eye
iridescent green-black head with a white neck ring
note: generic representative: a common/ring-necked pheasant male; the tail alone is longer than the body

name: Woodpecker
mustRead: straight chisel-shaped bill
body clinging vertically to a trunk
stiff pointed tail feathers braced against the bark
note: normally drawn clinging vertically, so it reads much taller than wide; the head is often crested or red-capped

name: Rat Snake
mustRead: long slender body with a flat-bottomed loaf cross-section
blunt rounded head barely wider than the neck
large round eyes with round pupils
note: generic representative: a black/corn rat snake; a harmless colubrid with no triangular viper head

name: Gecko
mustRead: huge lidless eyes with vertical pupils
broad splayed toes with lamellae pads
soft granular bumpy skin and a plump tail
note: most geckos cannot blink - the eyes are covered by a fixed clear scale and licked clean

name: Skink
mustRead: smooth glossy overlapping polished scales
cylindrical body with very small short legs
tapering tail as long as the body
note: generic representative: a typical ground skink; it looks polished and almost limbless, not spiky or crested

name: Black Bear
mustRead: straight facial profile with a tan muzzle
rump higher than the shoulders
tall rounded ears and short curved claws
note: no shoulder hump - the highest point is the hindquarters, the opposite of a brown bear

name: Brown Bear
mustRead: prominent muscular shoulder hump
dished concave face with a broad forehead
long straight pale digging claws
note: the shoulder hump is the diagnostic - it makes the front of the animal the tallest point

name: Wolf
mustRead: broad blocky head with erect triangular ears
long legs and a narrow deep chest
straight bushy tail carried level or low
note: the tail hangs straight and never curls over the back the way a husky's does

name: Coyote
mustRead: narrow pointed muzzle
large erect triangular ears
bushy tail carried low
note: Slighter and leggier than a wolf; tail hangs down rather than out.

name: Bobcat
mustRead: very short bobbed tail
cheek ruff of side whiskers
small black ear tufts
note: Tail is a stub of 3-4 head-widths' worth of body length, not a full cat tail.

name: Lynx
mustRead: long black ear tufts
flared facial ruff
oversized snowshoe paws and long hind legs

name: Elk
mustRead: sweeping backswept antler rack
dark shaggy neck mane
pale cream rump patch

name: Fox
mustRead: huge bushy white-tipped tail
sharp triangular ears
low slender body on black stockings
note: Read as red fox. Body is far lower and lighter than a dog's; the tail is nearly body-length.

name: Raccoon
mustRead: black bandit mask across the eyes
ringed banded tail
hunched arched back with rump higher than shoulders

name: Badger
mustRead: broad flattened low-slung body
white stripe running back over the face
long straight digging foreclaws

name: Weasel
mustRead: extremely long tube-like body
very short legs
small flat rounded ears
note: Body is serpentine, often drawn arched; the head is barely wider than the neck.

name: Stoat
mustRead: black-tipped tail
long tubular body
short legs and long neck

name: Mink
mustRead: glossy dark chocolate fur
elongate low body
white chin patch

name: Marten
mustRead: bushy full-length tail
pale orange throat bib
large rounded ears on a foxy face

name: Flying Squirrel
mustRead: loose skin flap stretched from wrist to ankle
flattened feather-like tail
enormous black eyes

name: Chipmunk
mustRead: bold dark and pale stripes along back and face
tail held up behind
bulging cheek pouches

name: Rabbit
mustRead: long upright ears
short round powder-puff tail
heavy crouched hind legs

name: Hare
mustRead: very long black-tipped ears
long rangy hind legs
lean angular body
note: Leggier and rangier than a rabbit, with proportionally much longer ears.

name: Mouse
mustRead: naked tail as long as the body
large round thin ears
pointed twitching snout

name: Vole
mustRead: stubby short tail
blunt rounded muzzle
ears half-buried in fur
note: Often drawn as a mouse; a vole is fatter, blunter-faced, short-tailed and small-eared.

name: Mole
mustRead: huge outward-turned spade forepaws
pink pointed fleshy snout
cylindrical neckless velvet body
note: No visible eyes or external ears; the forelimbs sit at the very front, almost beside the head.

name: Shrew
mustRead: long mobile pointed proboscis-like snout
tiny bead eyes
short velvety body and thin tail

name: Hedgehog
mustRead: dense cape of spines over the back
pointed pink snout poking out in front
rounded loaf-shaped body

name: Hawk
mustRead: hooked raptor beak with yellow cere
heavy scaled feet with curved talons
broad rounded wings folded over the back
note: Read as a generic buteo (red-tailed type). Perched profile is taller than wide; the body sits at a steep angle.

name: Crow
mustRead: all-black glossy plumage
stout straight pointed bill
square-tipped tail

name: Raven
mustRead: massive curved bill
shaggy throat hackles
wedge-shaped tail
note: Bigger-billed and shaggier-throated than a crow, with a wedge rather than a square tail.

name: Robin
mustRead: orange-red breast
upright plump posture
thin yellow bill
note: Read as American robin: a large thrush, not the tiny round European robin.

name: Cardinal
mustRead: pointed head crest
all-over scarlet plumage
black face mask around a thick conical orange bill

name: Turkey
mustRead: bare warty blue-and-red head with dangling wattle
broad fanned tail
bristly beard hanging from the breast

name: Garter Snake
mustRead: long pale stripes running the whole body length
slender limbless body
small head barely wider than the neck

name: Box Turtle
mustRead: high domed shell
hinged underside that shuts like a box
scaly clawed elephantine feet

name: Newt
mustRead: laterally flattened paddle tail
four small splayed limbs
moist granular skin

name: Frog
mustRead: bulging eyes set on top of the head
folded haunches with long hind legs
wide flat mouth line and no tail

name: Deer Tick
mustRead: eight legs bunched toward the front
flat teardrop unsegmented body
barbed spear mouthparts jutting ahead
note: Almost always drawn from above; in true side profile an unfed tick is a very low flat wedge. Eight legs, not six.

name: Bee
mustRead: furry thorax with banded amber-and-black abdomen
two pairs of clear veined wings
pollen basket on the hind leg
note: Read as a honeybee. Four wings, not two; the body is fuzzy, not smooth like a wasp's.

name: Earthworm
mustRead: ringed segmented tube body
swollen saddle band (clitellum) near the front
no limbs, eyes or head features

name: Fisher
mustRead: long low mustelid body with bushy tapering tail
dark grizzled coat
broad rounded ears and blunt muzzle

name: River Otter
mustRead: thick muscular tail tapering to a point
webbed feet
blunt whiskered face with small ears

name: Beaver
mustRead: flat scaly paddle tail
big orange chisel incisors
stocky humped body on short legs

name: Heron

mustRead: deeply forked tail streamers
long narrow pointed wings
slim dagger bill and a black cap over the crown

name: Auk
mustRead: upright penguin-like stance with black back and white front
small stubby wings held tight to the body
legs set far back at the rear of the body
note: Generic name read as a representative razorbill-type auk. Stands vertically, so it is taller than long.

name: Puffin
mustRead: huge triangular laterally flattened bill striped orange and blue-grey
big white face patch on a black cap
bright orange webbed feet

name: Guillemot
mustRead: long slender pointed dagger bill
upright chocolate-brown-and-white body
narrow head running smoothly into the neck

name: Eider Duck
mustRead: long wedge-shaped bill running in a straight line into the forehead
bulky heavy-bodied duck sitting low in the water
black-and-white blocks with a pale green nape
note: The unbroken sloping wedge from bill tip to crown is the key read; a normal duck's stepped forehead is wrong.

name: Arctic Cod
mustRead: slim elongated body with a deeply forked tail
small barbel under the chin
projecting upper jaw and large eye

name: Herring
mustRead: streamlined silver body with a keeled belly
single small dorsal fin at mid-back
deeply forked tail and large eye with an upturned jaw

name: Krill
mustRead: translucent shrimp-like body with visible feathery gills outside the shell
large stalked black eyes
fan of swimming legs under the abdomen

name: Copepod
mustRead: teardrop head-body wider at the front and tapering back
long outstretched antennae as wide as the body is long
forked bristly tail
note: Generic name read as a representative calanoid copepod. It has a single simple median eye spot, not paired stalked eyes.

name: Amphipod
mustRead: laterally flattened body curled into a C
many segmented legs of differing shapes along the underside
two pairs of antennae on a small head
note: Generic name read as a representative gammarid amphipod. It is squashed side to side, so the side view is the widest view.

name: Jellyfish
mustRead: translucent domed bell
long trailing tentacles hanging far below
frilled oral arms under the centre of the bell
note: Generic name read as a representative scyphozoan jellyfish. Tentacle length dominates the profile, making it much taller than wide.

name: Fur Seal
mustRead: small external ear flaps
very long fore-flippers propping the chest up
dog-like whiskered muzzle
note: Unlike a true seal it walks on all fours with hind flippers rotated forward.

name: Blue Whale
mustRead: tiny nub dorsal fin set far back near the tail
broad flat U-shaped rostrum with a single ridge
pleated throat grooves
note: Commonly drawn with a large dorsal fin; the real fin is a thumb-sized nub three-quarters back.

name: Humpback Whale
mustRead: enormously long white wing-like pectoral flippers
knobbly tubercles on the head and jaw
scalloped trailing edge on the tail flukes

name: Penguin
mustRead: fully upright standing posture on short rear-set feet
stiff flipper wings held flat at the sides
black back and white belly countershading

name: Albatross
mustRead: immensely long narrow stiff-held wings
heavy hooked bill with tube nostrils on the sides
short tail behind a bulky body
note: Wings are narrow and plank-straight, not broad and fingered like a raptor's.

name: Petrel
mustRead: tubular nostrils riding on top of the bill
narrow angled swept-back wings
compact gull-like body

name: Skua
mustRead: heavy hooked pirate bill
white flash at the base of the primaries
barrel-chested bulky gull build

name: Squid
mustRead: torpedo mantle with triangular fins at the pointed rear
eight arms plus two longer clubbed tentacles
large eye at the base of the arms

name: Octopus
mustRead: bulbous sack-like mantle above the eyes
eight tapering arms lined with suckers
horizontal slit pupil
note: The bulb is the mantle, not the head; the eyes sit below it, and there are no tentacles - eight equal arms only.

name: Starfish
mustRead: five tapering arms radiating from a small central disc
rows of tube feet in grooves underneath
pebbled granular skin
note: Headless radial animal - always read face-on; it has no true profile.

name: Sea Urchin
mustRead: spherical test bristling with long straight spines
five-part radial pattern under the spines

name: Sea Cucumber
mustRead: soft sagging sausage body
ring of branched feeding tentacles at the mouth end
rows of stubby tube feet along the underside

name: Cold-Water Fish
mustRead: stout torpedo body
soft-rayed dorsal fin and forked tail
blunt rounded snout with a chin barbel
note: Generic name - interpreted as a cod/char-type coldwater bony fish.

name: Monkey
mustRead: long curling tail as long as the body
grasping hands and feet with opposable thumbs
flat forward-facing face with round eyes
note: Generic name - interpreted as a macaque/capuchin-type monkey (tailed, not an ape).

name: Condor
mustRead: bare wrinkled unfeathered head
huge plank-broad wings with splayed fingered primaries
white ruff of feathers at the neck base

name: Bear
mustRead: muscular shoulder hump over the forelegs
small rounded ears on a broad dished head
flat-footed plantigrade paws and a stub tail

name: Swift
mustRead: scythe-shaped crescent wings swept far back
tiny bill with an enormous gape
cigar body with almost no visible legs
note: Often drawn as a swallow; the swift has stiffer sickle wings, a much shorter notched tail, and no long streamers.

name: Cave Snake
mustRead: limbless coiled rope body
pale washed-out unpigmented scales
blunt wedge head with heat-sensing pits
note: Generic name - interpreted as a pale cave-dwelling ratsnake/pitviper type.

name: Olm
mustRead: pale pink translucent eel-like body
bushy red external gills behind the head
tiny spindly legs with three toes
note: Eyes are skinned over and invisible; the limbs are vestigially thin, not lizard-like.

name: Blind Fish
mustRead: smooth blank eyeless head
pale pinkish unpigmented body
ordinary tetra-like fin layout

name: Cave Shrimp
mustRead: glassy translucent colourless body
extremely long sweeping antennae
curved segmented abdomen with a tail fan

name: Millipede
mustRead: cylindrical tube body of many identical rings
two pairs of short legs per segment in a rippling fringe
short clubbed antennae on a rounded head
note: Legs are short and hidden under the body, unlike a centipede's long splayed legs.

name: Snake
mustRead: limbless tapering body in S-curves
wedge head continuous with the neck
flicking forked tongue
note: Generic name - interpreted as a representative colubrid.

name: Wild Pig
mustRead: long wedge snout ending in a flat disc nose
high shoulder hump with a bristly crest mane
short upward-curving tusks

name: Small Fish
mustRead: simple streamlined silvery body
single dorsal fin mid-back
forked tail
note: Generic name - interpreted as a representative minnow-type baitfish.

name: Water Beetle
mustRead: smooth oval domed wing cases
flattened hair-fringed hind legs used as oars
short clubbed antennae on a tucked head

name: Fly Larvae
mustRead: legless soft segmented grub
tapered pointed head end and blunt rear
creamy white glossy skin

name: Grayling

small mouth on a trout-shaped body
adipose fin and forked tail

name: Minnow
mustRead: small slim silvery body
single soft dorsal fin set mid-back
dark lateral stripe

name: Sculpin

scaleless tapering tadpole-shaped body

name: Caddisfly

name: Mayfly

slender upcurved abdomen

name: Stonefly
mustRead: wings folded flat and overlapping down the back
two short stout tail cerci
long antennae on a flat squarish head

name: Gharial

tall laterally flattened paddle tail

name: Sturgeon

four barbels under a long pointed snout
shark-like upturned asymmetric tail

name: Paddlefish
mustRead: long flat paddle-shaped rostrum a third of the body length
cavernous gaping toothless mouth
smooth scaleless skin and shark-like tail

name: Perch
mustRead: two separate dorsal fins, the front one spiny
dark vertical bars down green-gold flanks
orange-red pelvic and anal fins

name: Pacu
mustRead: deep coin-shaped compressed body
blunt steep forehead with an underslung jaw
flat square human-like teeth

name: Arapaima

large armoured scales edged in red at the rear
bony flattened head with a small upward mouth

name: Arowana
mustRead: steeply upturned drawbridge mouth
two barbels projecting from the chin
long ribbon dorsal and anal fins running to the tail

name: Freshwater Shrimp
mustRead: curved segmented abdomen ending in a tail fan
long whip antennae from a spiked rostrum
small pincered front legs

name: Mussel

byssal beard threads anchoring it

flat whiskered head with short round ears

barrel body with front flippers and no hind limbs

long neck kinked back onto the shoulders

hooked bill and outsized barbed talons

name: Sunfish
mustRead: very deep round pancake-flat body

note: Ambiguous name - interpreted as a freshwater sunfish (bluegill type), not the oceanic mola.

white tip on the lower lobe of the tail

adipose fin behind the dorsal
large silvery scales and a deeply forked tail

name: Lungfish

name: Tigerfish

deeply forked red-tinged tail

name: Freshwater Crab
mustRead: squarish smooth carapace
two large pincers held forward
four pairs of jointed walking legs splayed sideways

name: Coot

sooty black rounded body
big lobed grey-green toes

name: Moorhen

white streak along the flank
white undertail flashes with a cocked tail

name: Goldfish
mustRead: stubby deep orange body
flowing double fan tail
high arched back with a long dorsal fin

name: Damselfly

hammerhead face with widely separated eyes

name: Water Strider

dimples denting the water surface under the feet
narrow slim boat-shaped body

silver air bubble held under the wing cases

name: Water Snail

broad muscular creeping foot
pair of slender head tentacles

thick hunched retractable neck

name: Mullet

long trailing filament off the rear of the dorsal fin

name: Shrimp

mustRead: long straight orange-red chisel bill
bold black-and-white blocked plumage
stout pink legs and a red eye ring

name: Coastal Lizard
mustRead: long tapering tail longer than the body

note: Generic name - interpreted as a rock/side-blotched lizard type.

one enlarged claw that plugs the shell mouth
stalked eyes and two pairs of antennae

name: Clam
mustRead: two symmetric hinged valves
concentric growth rings on the shell
pale muscular foot or paired siphons protruding

broad muscular creeping foot
head tentacles and a siphon tube

name: Sand Dollar

trapdoor plates at the summit
feathery cirri sweeping out of the opening

dense crown of soft waving tentacles
central mouth in the middle of the tentacle ring

crescent tail flukes held horizontally

name: Flounder

flat oval body fringed with a continuous fin skirt
twisted asymmetric mouth

name: Prawn
mustRead: long serrated rostrum spike over the eyes
curved segmented abdomen with a spread tail fan
very long whip antennae and slender legs

name: Marine Worm
mustRead: long segmented body fringed with bristly parapodia along both sides

long scaly rope-like tail
partly webbed hind feet
note: Generic name - interpreted as a muskrat/coypu type semi-aquatic rodent.

name: Godwit
mustRead: very long straight bill with a faint upward tilt and a pale base
long dark legs trailing behind in flight
cinnamon breast barred with dark chevrons

name: Avocet

crisp black-and-white pied patterning
long blue-grey legs

name: Mudskipper

arm-like pectoral fins propping the body up
two separate dorsal fins raised like sails

name: Fiddler Crab

name: Snail
mustRead: coiled spiral shell carried on the back
two long eye tentacles plus two short feelers
flat muscular gliding foot

name: Grouper
mustRead: huge cavernous mouth with a jutting lower jaw

rounded paddle tail

name: Mud Crab
mustRead: broad smooth fan-shaped carapace
heavy unequal crusher claws
flattened paddle-tipped rear legs

name: Dugong

name: Bonefish

name: Shark

name: Lobster

long whip antennae
segmented tail ending in a fan

name: Porpoise

stocky short body

name: Gannet

name: Cod

pale curved lateral line

name: Mackerel

narrow keeled tail stalk

name: Halibut

name: Reef Shark

sharply pointed wings, often white-spotted

name: Clownfish

blunt stubby snout

forked tail

name: Butterflyfish

dark bar masking the eye
pointed tweezer snout

name: Angelfish

name: Surgeonfish

long low dorsal fin running the whole back

name: Tang

small pointed grazing snout
crescent tail
note: same family as surgeonfish - drawn as a blue or yellow tang

name: Triggerfish

name: Parrotfish

round globular soft body with tiny fins

adipose fin before a forked tail

name: Dragonfish

eel-like black body with photophore rows

long trailing oar-like pelvic streamers and no tail fin

pinhead eyes right at the tip of the snout

name: Vampire Squid
mustRead: webbed cloak joining all eight arms into a cape
huge red-glowing eyes
pair of ear-like flap fins on the mantle

name: Deep-Sea Octopus
mustRead: ear-like fins flapping from the top of the mantle
webbed umbrella of skin between the eight arms
soft translucent gelatinous body
note: generic name - drawn as a finned dumbo-type deep-water octopus

name: Comb Jelly

transparent oval jelly body with no stinging tentacles

seven pairs of legs down the sides
large fixed compound eyes and two pairs of antennae

name: Tube Worm

feathery plume of tentacles fanning out of the tube mouth

name: Snailfish

sucker disc on the belly
fins merging into a tapering pointed tail

name: Isopod

two tail uropods flanking the rear plate
note: generic name - drawn as a representative marine isopod (woodlouse-like)

head bearing palps, antennae and an eversible jawed proboscis

bristle tufts poking out between the scales

name: Deep-Sea Fish

large light-gathering eyes
specks of photophores on a black soft body
note: generic name - drawn as a representative bathypelagic predator

name: Whale

blowhole on top of the head
long paddle flippers and a smooth streamlined body
note: generic name - drawn as a representative baleen whale; flukes are horizontal, never vertical like a fish

name: Monkfish

fleshy lure on the snout and frilly skin flaps along the jaw

cup polyps opening at the branch tips

name: Seabird

stout hooked or dagger bill
webbed feet
note: generic name - drawn as a representative gull

name: Iguana

banded tail far longer than the body

spiny crest along the nape and back
thick round tapering tail and stout clawed legs

name: Coconut Crab

stout red or yellow bill on a white pigeon-like body

chalk-white unpigmented skin
spindly toothpick legs

name: Cave Cricket

tiny eye turret on top of body

flat teardrop segmented abdomen
no tail and no sting
note: Commonly drawn with a stinging tail - it has none; the abdomen ends bluntly.

name: Cockroach
mustRead: flat glossy oval wing-covers
shield-shaped pronotum hiding the head
long backswept threadlike antennae

name: Flatworm

ribbon-flat unsegmented body
ear-like auricle lobes at the head corners

name: Insect-Eating Bat

large upright ears with a spike tragus
tiny hooked clinging feet

name: Cave Frog
mustRead: squat crouched body with folded hind legs
wide flat head as broad as the body
pale translucent depigmented skin
note: Generic - interpreted as a representative pale cave-dwelling frog; eyes reduced but still present and bulging.

name: Giant Centipede
mustRead: exactly one pair of legs per body segment
long trailing antennae and matching rear legs
curved venom claws under the head
note: One leg pair per segment, not two - that would be a millipede; body is flattened, not tubular.

name: Snow Petrel
mustRead: entirely pure white plumage
short black hooked bill with tube nostrils
long narrow pointed seabird wings

name: Mite
mustRead: featureless bag-like unsegmented body
eight short legs bunched at the front
tiny protruding mouth cone
note: Generic - interpreted as a typical dust/velvet mite. No waist, no separate head, no visible eyes.

name: Ice Worm
mustRead: thread-thin dark segmented body
no limbs at all
blunt rounded head end
note: A glacier annelid, black-brown and barely a few centimetres long - not a legged larva.

name: Cow
mustRead: heavy sagging barrel body with visible udder
hanging throat dewlap
sideways-set ears with tufted tail

name: Bull
mustRead: massive humped neck and shoulder mass
short forward-curving horns
heavy pendulous dewlap

name: Horse
mustRead: long arched neck with crest mane
single hoof on each long slim leg
long flowing tail from a high dock

name: Donkey
mustRead: very long upright ears
short upright bristly mane
cow-like tail tufted only at the tip
note: Straighter back, bigger head and shorter neck than a horse; no flowing forelock.

name: Pig
mustRead: flat round snout disc
deep barrel body on very short legs
curly corkscrew tail

name: Chicken
mustRead: plump rounded body on scaly legs
small comb and wattles
short upswept fan of tail feathers

name: Rooster
mustRead: tall red comb and long wattles
arching sickle tail plumes
upright puffed chest with hackle cape

name: Kestrel
mustRead: hooked bill with dark moustache stripe
rufous back spotted with black
long barred tail and pointed falcon wings
note: Slim and small-headed - not the bulky broad-winged silhouette of a hawk or buzzard.

name: Starling
mustRead: glossy iridescent black plumage flecked with pale spots
sharp straight pointed bill
short square tail with triangular wings

name: Llama
mustRead: long banana-curved ears
long upright S-curved neck
flat back with no hump
note: A camelid with no hump - larger, longer-faced and less woolly than an alpaca.

name: Alpaca
mustRead: dense woolly fleece covering the whole body
blunt short face under a topknot fringe
short straight spear-shaped ears

name: Moth
mustRead: feathery comb-like antennae
thick furry body
broad dusty wings held roof-like over the back
note: Generic - interpreted as a representative large-bodied nocturnal moth. Antennae are feathered or thread-like, never clubbed like a butterfly's.

name: Wasp
mustRead: pinched thread-thin waist
yellow-and-black banded pointed abdomen
narrow smooth hairless wings
note: Sleek and shiny - do not draw the fat furry body of a bee.

name: Aphid
mustRead: soft pear-shaped bulbous body
pair of tube-like cornicles on the rear
needle beak stuck into a stem

name: Dog
mustRead: muzzle ending in a black nose
erect or folded ears
plumed tail carried above the back
note: Generic - interpreted as a mid-sized domestic dog of no particular breed.

name: Fly
mustRead: huge red compound eyes filling the head
only two clear wings plus knob halteres
bristly grey-striped thorax

name: Carrion Beetle
mustRead: flat oval elytra blotched black and orange
clubbed knobbed antennae
abdomen tip left exposed past the short wing-covers

name: Cold-Adapted Insect

reduced or absent wings
note: Generic - interpreted as a representative polar/alpine insect (snow fly or Antarctic midge type): small, dark, hairy and flightless.

name: Desert Owl
mustRead: flat facial disc with huge forward-facing eyes
pale sandy-buff plumage
feathered legs and hooked bill nearly hidden in face feathers
note: Generic - interpreted as a pale desert-dwelling owl (desert tawny owl type). Owls are taller than wide when perched.

name: Vine Snake

long pointed dart-shaped snout
horizontal keyhole-shaped pupils

black fur with a white chest band
thick short tapering tail on a low stocky body

note: Shorter-faced, smaller and more compact than a kangaroo; the body is more hunched and rabbit-like.

name: Sugar Glider

long bushy tail as long as the body

long bushy tail on a low slinking body

name: Gila Monster

blunt heavy head on a thick neck

bright orange-gold staring eyes
note: Generic - interpreted as the ring-tailed lemur, the representative member of the group.

heavy squat flightless parrot body

two-forward two-back gripping toes

dished concave facial profile

steel-blue scales flecked with white

leathery hood over the head

eight stubby clawed legs including a rear-facing pair
telescoping tube mouth at the front

long rigid spike tail
all legs concealed beneath the shell

slim deep-chested body on fine legs

white face with a dark eye stripe

name: Bongo

white chevron between the eyes

name: Duiker

very small antelope on short legs
note: Generic - interpreted as a representative forest duiker; the crouching hump-backed posture is diagnostic.

name: Gerenuk

name: Nilgai

back sloping down from high shoulders

stocky goat body on short strong legs

dark brown eye stripe on a whitish head
stocky short-tailed compact body

name: Weaverbird

clinging upside down to a woven grass nest
note: Generic - interpreted as a representative male village/southern masked weaver in breeding plumage.

name: Screamer

tiny round puckered beak mouth

name: Remora

slim dark torpedo body
jutting lower jaw and low fins set far back
note: The sucker is on the top of the head, not the belly - it is a modified dorsal fin.

name: Archerfish

dorsal fin set far back near the tail

name: Knifefish

body tapering to a blade-thin pointed tail
note: Generic - interpreted as a representative gymnotiform/ghost knifefish. It swims forwards and backwards with the undulating belly fin, body held rigid.

name: Icefish
mustRead: translucent white bloodless body with visible internal structure

large fan pectoral fins on scaleless skin

name: Mudminnow

translucent tunic showing internal basket

note: Headless and eyeless; often drawn as a chain of linked individuals.

name: Pyrosome

note: A colony, not one animal - a soft open-ended cone with no head, limbs or symmetry cues.

name: Lancelet
mustRead: translucent blade-shaped body pointed at both ends
rows of V-shaped muscle chevrons visible through the skin
fringe of oral tentacles where a head would be
note: Has no head, no jaws and no eyes - just a stiffening notochord line running end to end.

name: Sea Spider
mustRead: body reduced to a thin stick between the legs
enormously long spindly legs holding the organs
long tubular sucking proboscis at the front
note: Not a spider - the body is so shrunken the gut and gonads extend into the legs; four eyes sit on a small turret.

name: Fairy Shrimp
mustRead: swims upside down on its back
eleven pairs of leaf-like legs beating in a wave
stalked eyes on a translucent shell-less body
note: Has no carapace at all - the body is a bare translucent tube; often orange or pink toward the tail.

name: Tadpole Shrimp
mustRead: broad flat shield carapace covering the front half
two long thin forked tail filaments
dozens of wriggling leaf legs beneath the shield
note: Two dark eyes sit close together on top of the shield, giving it a helmeted look.

name: Springtail
mustRead: stubby soft six-legged body
forked jumping furcula folded under the abdomen
short beaded antennae
note: Not an insect proper - wingless with only six abdominal segments and a spring-loaded tail latch.

name: Dobsonfly
mustRead: huge crossed sickle mandibles in the male
long smoky net-veined wings folded well past the abdomen
soft elongated flabby body

name: Scorpionfly
mustRead: long downward beak-like snout with jaws at the tip
bulbous upcurled scorpion-like tail tip in the male
narrow wings blotched with black
note: The upturned tail is harmless male genitalia, not a sting.

name: Thrips
mustRead: slender cigar-shaped body
narrow strap wings fringed with long hairs
asymmetrical cone-shaped rasping mouth
